RLA - Regulation of Lobbying Act 1040/81: parallel single-page codification of the same Article 1-A act (full text, ~52KB, no section-leaf children). Lossy fallback / cross-codification; the 22 leg/ section leaves are the canonical bodies.

notes: NY 2010 available on Justia; Cloudflare clear, no challenges. NY's lobbying-disclosure regime is the Legislative Law Article 1-A 'Lobbying Act' (Regulation of Lobbying Act, Ch. 1040/81; sections 1-A through 1-V). Justia codifies this SAME statute under multiple parallel paths: leg/ (Legislative Law - canonical), rla/ (Regulation of Lobbying Act), and a cross-reference under exc/ (Executive Law). CODIFICATION PATH CHOSEN: leg/article-1-a/ as primary. Pass-1 selected leg/ and rla/; pass-2 on leg/ identified Article 1-A (labeled LOBBYING ACT, range 1-A - 1-V); pass-3 on leg/article-1-a/ recursed into 22 distinct section-leaf URLs (1-A..1-V), each a separate statute section body. These 22 leaves are the core_chapter set and are the non-lossy canonical bodies the prior 5/15 pilot missed. The rla/ title page returned an EMPTY pass-2 TSV: it is a single monolithic page (~52KB visible text, 73 'Lobbyist' mentions, registration/expenditure/penalty language present) with NO section-leaf child links - the 'single-page codified act' convention (example C in pass-2 prompt) and the lossy stub the dispatch warned about. It is included once as support_chapter so the full act text is recoverable, but the leg/ section leaves are preferred for granular extraction. exc/ (Executive Law) deliberately excluded as a cross-reference stub. SECTION-LEAF URLs REACHED: 22 (all under leg/article-1-a/). tree_depth=5: new-york -> 2010 -> leg -> article-1-a -> <section>.
